canonical_name: Existence and construction of expander graphs (exact proposition open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 扩展图的存在性与构造
literal_source_claim_en: Existence and construction of expander graphs.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not select vertex, edge, conductance, or spectral expansion; a graph and family model; degree and expansion constants; subset and normalization conventions; order and size quantifiers; an infinite-family requirement; or probabilistic, explicit, algorithmic, or computable construction. Choosing a standard bounded-degree uniform-expansion theorem or a named construction would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the graph model and vertex universe, finite-family/index encoding, cardinality and coefficient domains, regularity/degree conditions, expansion measure and normalization, and all required decidability, finiteness, order, matrix, and spectral structures.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not say whether the target proves existence for one graph, selected orders, all sufficiently large orders, infinitely many orders, or an unbounded family, nor what probabilistic, explicit, uniform, algorithmic, or computable construction guarantee is required.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake because no proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every graph, parameter, subset, size, family, construction, and boundary case listed below and in scope-map.md.
candidate_scope_not_credited: existence of finite vertex expanders with a fixed regular degree and uniform positive external-neighborhood expansion
existence of finite edge expanders or conductance expanders with fixed bounded degree
existence of regular spectral expanders with a stated adjacency or normalized-Laplacian eigenvalue gap
an unbounded infinite family of uniformly expanding bounded-degree graphs
a randomized existence theorem with a quantified success probability
an explicit algebraic, algorithmic, or computable expander-family construction
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, and other small vertex types, including orders below the stated degree
degree zero, one, or two and disconnected or isolated-vertex graphs
empty, full, proper, and exactly-half-sized tested subsets and odd-cardinality rounding
zero or negative real expansion constants and strict versus non-strict inequalities
external versus closed neighborhoods and whether boundary vertices inside the tested set count
every order versus sufficiently large orders, infinitely many orders, or a selected subsequence
exact graph order versus a lower bound and bounded versus unbounded family orders
repeated or isomorphic family members, labels, connectedness, regularity, and uniformity
nonconstructive existence versus randomized, explicit, uniform, algorithmic, or computable construction
excluded_substitutions: THM-M-0882 Margulis construction, THM-M-0883 Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak construction, THM-M-0884 Ramanujan graphs, THM-M-0885 Morgenstern's theorem, or THM-M-0886 Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava
a single complete graph or other finite example substituted for an unbounded expander family
a vertex-expansion theorem substituted for edge or spectral expansion, or conversely, without checked relationships
a structure or predicate whose fields assume the requested expansion or construction conclusion
generic finite-graph, regularity, adjacency-matrix, Laplacian, or connectivity APIs without an exact source-mapped theorem bridge
random graph sampling, numerical spectrum computation, or empirical expansion checks
the catalog's untrusted verified label, a title match, cluster context, or a bounded discovery query used as proof evidence
